descriptions.startState: Stand upright with both feet grounded, body centered over the feet, arms relaxed beside the torso.
descriptions.targetShape: Tall neutral standing posture with feet grounded, knees long but not forcefully locked, pelvis stacked under rib cage, spine long, head balanced over trunk, arms relaxed by the sides.
segmentRelationships: head remains stacked over rib cage and pelvis
left and right shoulders stay level
hips remain centered between both feet
knees track in the same direction as feet
trajectory: settle weight evenly across both feet
lengthen from pelvis through crown without leaning
allow shoulders and arms to settle naturally
transitionOut: remain standing and release any deliberate postural tension
visualAcceptance: arms hang naturally without clipping torso

descriptions.startState: Begin in Mountain Pose with both feet planted and trunk tall.
descriptions.targetShape: Bend hips and knees as if sitting back into a chair while keeping both feet planted; torso inclines only as needed for balance; arms reach overhead without shrugging or crossing the head.
segmentRelationships: pelvis moves back and down between the feet
knees flex and track with toes
rib cage stays organized over pelvis
upper arms remain close to the ear/head line
elbows stay straight
trajectory: hips travel posteriorly and downward
knees flex together
ankles dorsiflex while heels stay grounded
arms elevate smoothly to overhead
return by reversing the same path
orientation: gaze forward or slightly ahead of floor without forcing neck extension

lowerBody: front hip and knee flex as in the standing portion of a lunge
rear knee remains long and does not descend toward the floor
pelvis remains centered between the two planted feet
trunk: chest opens toward the long side of the stance
torso remains tall instead of pitching over the front thigh
arms: both arms travel laterally outward from their own shoulders
front arm reaches in the same general direction as the front foot
rear arm reaches in the opposite direction
arms finish approximately horizontal at shoulder height
head: head rotates toward the front arm and gaze continues over the front fingertips
prohibitedTrajectories: rear knee dropping toward the floor
either arm sweeping behind the torso before reaching shoulder height
arms crossing the chest or head
torso folding forward over the front thigh

descriptions.startState: Begin standing tall with both feet under the body and arms relaxed; prepare to step into a wide split stance.
descriptions.targetShape: A stationary-lunge-style lower body with the front knee bent and the rear leg straight, combined with an upright side-open torso and two straight arms reaching in opposite directions at shoulder height.
segmentRelationships: front knee stacks toward the front ankle and tracks with the front toes
rear knee stays extended and rear leg remains long
pelvis stays between both planted feet
torso stays upright while chest opens to the side
left and right arms form one long shoulder-height line through the shoulders
head turns independently toward the front hand
trajectory: step feet wide apart
orient the front foot toward the front end and the rear foot at a stable outward angle
bend the front knee using stationary-lunge mechanics while keeping the rear knee straight
open pelvis and chest toward the long side
sweep both arms laterally outward from the shoulders until they reach shoulder height
turn head toward the front hand
orientation: front toes point toward the front end
rear foot stays angled and fully grounded
palms face down or near-neutral toward the floor
arms point in opposite horizontal directions
transitionIn: front knee bends while rear leg stays long
arms move laterally outward to shoulder height
transitionOut: lower arms laterally toward sides without sweeping behind body
visualAcceptance: rear knee never drops toward floor
arms extend straight from shoulders in opposite directions
arms do not travel behind torso

lowerBody: hips travel upward and backward away from the planted hands
knees lengthen only as far as the spine can remain long
heels reach toward the floor without requiring contact
trunk: spine lengthens from pelvis toward shoulders and hands
pelvis is the highest point of the target shape
arms: hands stay planted in front of the shoulders
shoulders move back relative to fixed hands as hips rise
upper arms remain in front of the torso and lengthen toward the hands
biceps finish beside the ears rather than behind the back
head: head remains between the upper arms with neck relaxed and continuous with the spine
prohibitedTrajectories: hands moving behind the shoulder line
elbows bending into a backward swimming motion
hips dropping into a crouch instead of lifting back and up

descriptions.startState: Begin from a stable hands-and-knees or high-plank-compatible four-point setup with both hands planted in front of the shoulders and both feet prepared to bear weight.
descriptions.targetShape: An inverted V supported by both hands and both feet: hips lift high and backward, spine lengthens, arms stay straight and forward from the shoulders toward the fixed hands, and legs lengthen only as far as comfortable.
segmentRelationships: hands remain in front of shoulders and do not slide
shoulders-to-hands form a long forward support line
upper arms stay near the ear line rather than rotating behind the torso
hips become the highest point
spine lengthens from hands through shoulders toward pelvis
knees may stay softly bent to preserve spinal length
head remains between the upper arms
trajectory: keep both hands fixed on the floor in front of the shoulders
press through hands and feet
move pelvis upward and backward
allow shoulders to travel backward relative to the planted hands while arms stay straight
lengthen the spine
gradually lengthen knees without changing the forward arm-support line
orientation: fingers point forward or slightly outward
transitionIn: shoulders move away from hands while elbows stay straight
transitionOut: keep hands in front of shoulders until returning to supported transition
visualAcceptance: all four support contacts remain stable
arms remain long and in front of torso
spine does not collapse into rounded crouch

lowerBody: legs stay long behind the body
pelvis and lower trunk remain supported by the floor
trunk: sternum travels forward first and then upward
upper spine extends while pelvis stays down
lift comes from chest and spinal extension rather than moving the whole root upward
arms: hands stay planted beside the lower ribs or shoulders
upper arms stay close to the sides of the torso
elbows point backward beside the ribs as they gradually extend
shoulders move forward and upward relative to the fixed hands
head: head follows the upper spine and gaze moves forward/slightly upward without throwing the head back
prohibitedTrajectories: hands sliding backward behind the shoulders
upper arms sweeping behind the torso
head snapping backward independently of the spine

descriptions.startState: Begin prone with legs extended behind, pelvis and lower trunk supported, and palms planted beside the lower ribs or shoulders with elbows bent and pointing backward beside the torso.
descriptions.targetShape: A prone spinal-extension shape in which the hands stay fixed, pelvis and legs stay grounded, chest glides forward and upward, upper arms remain beside the ribs, and elbows extend only as much as needed for the lifted chest.
segmentRelationships: pelvis remains grounded while chest rises
legs stay long and parallel behind body
palms remain beside the rib/shoulder line rather than behind it
upper arms stay close to torso
elbows track backward beside ribs
shoulders remain away from ears
head follows the upper spine
supports: left and right legs supported by floor
trajectory: keep palms fixed beside lower ribs/shoulders
press tops of feet and pelvis into the floor
draw sternum forward before lifting it upward
allow shoulders to travel forward/up relative to the fixed hands
let elbows extend gradually while continuing to point backward beside ribs
return by bending elbows and lowering chest forward/down
orientation: gaze moves forward/slightly upward with neck continuous with spine
transitionOut: return torso toward mat while pelvis stays grounded
visualAcceptance: hands do not slide behind shoulders
upper arms stay beside torso instead of sweeping backward

descriptions.startState: Begin supine with knees bent, feet planted near the pelvis, arms long beside the torso and head/shoulders resting on the floor.
descriptions.targetShape: Lift pelvis until shoulders, hips and knees form a controlled rising line while feet, shoulders, upper arms and head remain supported; knees remain approximately hip-width and point forward.
segmentRelationships: knees stay aligned over or toward ankles
left and right thighs remain roughly parallel
pelvis lifts without knees splaying
rib cage and pelvis rise as one controlled bridge rather than hyperextending the lumbar spine
shoulders/head remain supported
arms stay long by sides
trajectory: press both feet into floor
posteriorly organize pelvis without force
lift pelvis upward
extend hips while knees stay bent
hold
lower spine/pelvis under control
transitionOut: keep feet planted until fully down
